newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swastikas painted on Grass's office, German church.
newsitem.headline: Swastikas painted on Grass's office, German church.

text.p: Vandals spray-painted swastikas on the office of Germany's most famous author Guenter Grass and on a church in the latest in a series of extremist attacks in northern Germany, authorities said on Wednesday.
Two white swastikas were painted on the entrance to the building, Grass's secretary told police.
Grass is the author of The Tin Drum and many other popular novels. Long associated with the left-leaning Social Democratic Party, he was an outspoken opponent of German unification.
Prosecutor Heinrich Wille said the perpetrators were not necessarily neo-Nazis, but might just be attention-seekers.

Authorities said they saw no evidence of a connection with an arson attack on a Catholic church in the same town at the end of May, although swastikas had also been sprayed on the walls around that church.
A 19-year-old apprentice is under arrest as a suspect in that case.
Several other churches in northern Germany have recently been the targets of arson attempts.

In a separate incident in the eastern city of Dresden, police are investigating 13 juvenile right-wing suspects in the robbery of a group of visitors to a church convention last week. Four of the 13 have confessed, police said.
